title: Name Trinity; persons; one essence three subsistences
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): by means belonging toward reason belonging toward a certain property plus relation — yet they stand as distinct not by means belonging toward reason alone but in ye thing itself. Person with ye relations by means belonging toward that same which they stand as constituted stand as subsistences — John 14. There stand as not three Gods, three Lords, plus so on. Thus ye orthodox fathers established ye distinction out from ye words ousia plus hypostasis. 1 John 5:7. Father, Son, plus Holy Spirit, not three Gods, because ye essence or deity stands as one — Colossians 2:9; — but there stand as three persons. 14. incommunicable, living, understanding, willing, powerful, acting — John 5; — a person in God stands as a hypostasis or individual subsistence. Moreover, by means belonging toward ye word Trinity here we do not signify a ternary numbering number simply, but persons distinct in one essence.
pass_b_english: Moreover, by the word Trinity here we do not signify a ternary numbering number simply, but persons distinct in one essence. A person in God is a hypostasis or individual subsistence, incommunicable, living, understanding, willing, powerful, acting — John 5; 14.

But there are three persons, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, not three Gods, because the essence or deity is one — Colossians 2:9; 1 John 5:7. Thus the orthodox fathers established the distinction from the words ousia and hypostasis. There are not three Gods, three Lords, and so on.
Person with the relations by which they are constituted are subsistences — John 14. Yet they are distinct not by reason alone but in the thing itself, by reason of a certain property and relation.
source_text: Caeterum, voce Trinitatis hic non numerum ternarium numerantem simpliciter, sed personas in una essentia distinctas significamus. Persona in Deo est hypostasis seu subsistentia individua, incommunicabilis, viva, intelligens, volens, potens, agens — Joh. V; XIV. Sunt autem tres personae, Pater, Filius et Spiritus Sanctus, non tres Dei, quia una est essentia seu deitas — Col. II.9; I Joh. V.7. Sic orthodoxi patres e voce ousia et hypostasis distinctionem constituerunt. Non sunt tres Dei, tres Domini, etc. Persona cum relationibus quibus constituuntur subsistentes sunt — Joh. XIV. Non sola tamen ratione, sed reipsa distinctae, di ratione cujusdam proprietatis et relationis.
